newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AKRAM BRAVES PAIN TO CLINCH SERIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AKRAM BRAVES PAIN TO CLINCH SERIES.

text.p: Pakistan captain Wasim Akram shrugged off injury to spearhead a fast bowling rout of West Indies on Monday to clinch the World Series Cup then declared his side were the best one-day team in the world.

Pakistan routed West Indies for 103 in an outstanding bowling display to win by 62 runs and take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the best-of-three final. It was the Pakistanis' first win in the triangular limited overs tournamemt.
"We told everyone when we arrived in Australia that we are the best team in the world. We have won the competition and we have got a young team that is very talented," Akram said.
Not even a power failure that left the stadium in darkness for 24 minutes could distract Akram and his team from their task.

Despite a niggling hamstring strain, Akram generated extreme pace, bounce and movement off the seam to dismiss opener Sherwin Campbell and middle order pair Shivnarine Chanderpaul and Carl Hooper in sweltering temperatures.
"I pulled the hamstring in my second or third over and I was just about to come off when I got two wickets in one over. At times, it was very painful," Akram added.
"We have come to Australia before and got hammered in this tournament, so this is a big highlight for Pakistan cricket.''

Fellow fast bowler Shahid Nazir, drafted into the side to replace leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed, justified his selection by exploiting a lively pitch to finish with outstanding figures of three for 14 from his 10 overs.
Pakistan beat West Indies by four wickets in the first final in Sydney on Saturday.
West Indies captain Courtney Walsh, already concerned about his side's batting frailty, watched a second successive collapse.
After losing seven wickets for the addition of 24 runs in Sydney, West Indies were reduced to 42 for seven when vice-captain Brian Lara fell for 19.
Ijaz Ahmed, the top scorer in Pakistan's victory in Sydney, scored 45 to bolster the middle order, while Mohammad Wasim hit 41 in the final overs off 79 balls.
